title: Good as food scale only; app not ready for prime time
text:
Good as food scale only; app not ready for prime time. It comes with the scale, 4 AAA batteries (only 3 are needed), and a small setup manual that does not describe how to operate the app.

Based on my tests, I consider this a nice food scale that is only slightly quirky. It measures in grams, milliliter, milk volume when in milliliter, fluid ounces, and pounds and ounces. When using fluid ounces, it changes quickly to pounds and ounces unless I put something on the scale immediately. That is the quirky part.

I also downloaded the Android version of the Foodiet on my Samsung Galaxy Tab. I had to create an account and accept all the privacy and grant access to everything (photos, etc.) before I could continue. I then have to enter my sex, weight, and height and my goal weight. It has the ability to read package barcodes but what it read was garbage (see one photo where my package of nuts was labeled "Emmental" with totally wrong calories). I could also search for the foods and add them in as my breakfast, lunch, dinner, or snacks. I could also establish a meal plan. However, the app was usually non-responsive when I tried to navigate through it. It was not totally intuitive and did not always register the weight of items when I asked it to take the weight.

In summary, the app is useless to me and also requires a tremendous amount of time to set up. As a scale only, I would give this 4.5 stars. As a Smart scale, this gets 1 star, hence the 3-star rating. The current price of $29.99 is about $10 too much for this scale considering the app side does not work well.
